row.description: The commercial AWS partition convention for naming an S3 bucket resource is arn:aws:s3:::bucket-name. S3 bucket ARNs deliberately leave the region and account components empty.

neighbors.relation: same ARN family, but account is mandatory
same service, but includes region and account

row.wrong_generalization: A wrong generalization is to require every AWS ARN to contain nonempty region and account fields. S3 bucket ARNs use the same colon-separated ARN shape but intentionally leave both fields blank.

row.description: An API Gateway route method is an IANA-registered HTTP method token, such as GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, CONNECT, or TRACE.

neighbors.relation: paired with a method to form an API route
another HTTP-layer field but numeric rather than lexical

row.wrong_generalization: A wrong generalization is to accept any uppercase alphabetic token as an HTTP method. Route configuration should use the IANA HTTP-method vocabulary rather than treating arbitrary verbs as valid methods.

row.description: S3 object keys are flat strings, but console and tooling conventions use slash-terminated repeated segments as a folder-style prefix, for example logs/2025/.

neighbors.relation: the complete flat key that may begin with this prefix
similar visual notation but different hierarchy semantics

row.wrong_generalization: A wrong generalization is to treat S3 prefixes as actual filesystem directories. The slash is part of the object-key string; the repeated slash-terminated form is a useful listing convention, not a server-enforced directory hierarchy.
